description.p: OpenMac emulates four Macintosh computers: the Macintosh Classic, the Macintosh IIfx, the Quadra 650 and the Quadra 950. Each machine has its own processor core, video, storage, input, sound and parameter RAM, written from scratch from public documentation.

OpenMac contains no original Macintosh code. You supply the ROM of the machine you own and your own system disks. Floppy images, hard disk images, CD images and host folders can be used as disks, and files can be passed in and out through a drop box folder.

The disk an archive dropped on the window rides in on can be taken off the Mac again, with File ▸ Remove Dropped Disk or by dragging its icon to the Trash. The Quadra 950 keeps its settings between sessions, and the Macintosh IIfx keeps a dropped archive's disk through a restart.

The Macintosh Quadra 950 joins as a fourth machine. Floppy fixes on the Macintosh IIfx, corrected 12-inch and 21-inch displays on the Quadra 650, and the window stays on the display when the Mac's screen changes size.
The Quadra 650 starts up from a CD and shows thousands of colors. Restart fixes on the Quadra 650 and the Macintosh IIfx. Version numbers now match OpenMac for Windows.
